answer: An agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable stake before it can vote on a job’s result. A randomly selected, independently staked jury checks the submitted evidence; if it finds fraud, the stake is slashed and split among honest reporters. Spawning a hundred sybils then means locking a hundred stakes, while coordination risks losing them all. The fable of free identities breaks at this vertex: each crystal-clear claim must carry capital at risk. This raises the attack’s cost, though it cannot stop a wealthy attacker or colluding jurors outright.
